cities.name: Sydney
cities.tagline: Harbour city of beaches, ferries, and sandstone headlands
cities.general: Sydney wraps a world-famous harbour with surf beaches, coastal walks, ferry rides, and national-park headlands. It is the natural starting point for east-coast journeys, Blue Mountains day trips, and food-led city stays.
activities: Ride the ferry to Manly at sunset
Explore The Rocks and Circular Quay
Take a day trip into the Blue Mountains
tips: Use an Opal or contactless card for ferries and trains
Book harbour restaurants ahead on weekends
Beach conditions change quickly; swim between the flags

cities.name: Melbourne
cities.tagline: Laneway culture, galleries, trams, and Great Ocean Road access
cities.general: Melbourne is Australia's culture capital: laneway cafes, street art, live music, major galleries, and easy tram travel. It also anchors road trips to the Great Ocean Road, Phillip Island, the Yarra Valley, and the Grampians.
activities: Follow a laneway coffee and street-art walk
Ride the tram to St Kilda Pier
Visit the NGV and Federation Square
Start a Great Ocean Road drive
tips: Weather can swing in a day; carry layers
The free tram zone covers central sights
Reserve popular restaurants before Friday and Saturday nights

cities.name: Brisbane
cities.tagline: Subtropical river city between islands and rainforest hinterland
cities.general: Brisbane follows the bends of the Brisbane River with galleries, riverside dining, bike paths, and easy access to Moreton Bay islands. It is a practical base for Lamington, the Scenic Rim, and south-east Queensland beaches.
activities: Walk South Bank and the riverfront
tips: Summer storms can be sudden
Use go card or contactless payment on public transport
Book island ferries during school holidays

cities.name: Perth
cities.tagline: Indian Ocean beaches, Swan River sunsets, and Rottnest escapes
cities.general: Perth pairs Indian Ocean beaches with a relaxed riverfront city, Kings Park views, Fremantle heritage, and short ferry rides to Rottnest Island. It is the west-coast launch point for wine regions, coral coast drives, and the Cape to Cape Track.
activities: Explore Fremantle's markets and heritage streets
Ride a ferry to Rottnest Island
tips: Distances in Western Australia are large; plan fuel stops
Book Rottnest ferries and bikes early in summer
A hat and sun protection are essential year-round

cities.name: Adelaide
cities.tagline: Parkland city for wine valleys, beaches, and festivals
cities.general: Adelaide is a compact city ringed by parklands and close to beaches, the Adelaide Hills, Barossa, McLaren Vale, and Kangaroo Island. Its markets, festivals, and wine access make it an easy South Australia base.
activities: Taste wine in the Adelaide Hills
Plan a Kangaroo Island side trip
tips: Festival season fills rooms quickly
Wine tours are easiest with a designated driver or guide
Summer heat can be extreme inland

cities.name: Canberra
cities.tagline: Planned capital of museums, lake loops, and bushland ridges
cities.general: Canberra is Australia's planned capital, built around Lake Burley Griffin and framed by bushland hills. National museums, parliament, galleries, cycling paths, and nearby Namadgi National Park make it a thoughtful inland stop.
activities: Visit Parliament House and the National Gallery
Climb Mount Ainslie for the city axis view
tips: Winter mornings are cold and frosty
Many national institutions are free
A car helps for nature reserves and suburban dining

cities.name: Hobart
cities.tagline: Tasmanian harbour capital below kunanyi / Mount Wellington
cities.general: Hobart sits between the Derwent River and kunanyi / Mount Wellington, with Georgian streets, Salamanca markets, ferries, MONA, and access to southern Tasmania's wild coast and convict heritage.
activities: Climb or drive to kunanyi / Mount Wellington
Visit Port Arthur as a day trip
tips: Mountain weather is colder than the waterfront
Book Bruny Island and Port Arthur tours ahead
Saturday market mornings are busiest

cities.name: Darwin
cities.tagline: Top End gateway for markets, sunsets, Kakadu, and Litchfield
cities.general: Darwin is the tropical Top End capital, known for waterfront sunsets, markets, World War II history, and access to Kakadu, Litchfield, and Arnhem Land touring.
activities: Visit the Museum and Art Gallery of the Northern Territory
Use Darwin as a Kakadu launch point
tips: The dry season from May to September is most comfortable
Observe crocodile warning signs around waterways
Many remote trips require permits or guided access

cities.name: Cairns
cities.tagline: Reef and rainforest base in tropical Far North Queensland
cities.general: Cairns is the main base for Great Barrier Reef trips, Wet Tropics rainforest, Kuranda rail journeys, and Daintree excursions. The city is compact, tour-friendly, and built around tropical outdoor travel.
activities: Take a reef snorkel or dive day trip
tips: Reef boats book out in school holidays
Marine stinger season usually runs November to May
Summer is humid and wet; carry rain protection

cities.name: Gold Coast
cities.tagline: Surf beaches, skyline stays, and rainforest hinterland trails
cities.general: The Gold Coast mixes surf beaches and high-rise resorts with rainforest hinterland parks, waterfalls, and family attractions. It is a bright, easy stop between Brisbane and northern New South Wales.
tips: Swim only between flags
Weekend traffic builds around theme parks
Hinterland roads can be misty after rain

cities.name: Alice Springs
cities.tagline: Red Centre town for desert ranges and Larapinta Trail access
cities.general: Alice Springs is the practical hub of Australia's Red Centre, backed by the MacDonnell Ranges and the Larapinta Trail. It works best for self-drive desert trips, Aboriginal art, and outback landscapes.
activities: Walk sections of the Larapinta Trail
Visit the Alice Springs Desert Park
tips: Carry far more water than you expect to need
Avoid exposed hikes in midday heat
Remote-road fuel and supplies need planning

cities.name: Auckland
cities.tagline: Harbour city of volcanic cones, islands, and Pacific food
cities.general: Auckland spreads across twin harbours, volcanic cones, island ferries, black-sand surf beaches, and diverse Pacific dining. It is New Zealand's biggest gateway and a flexible start for North Island journeys.
activities: Climb Mount Eden for crater and skyline views
Take a ferry to Waiheke Island
Walk the waterfront and Wynyard Quarter
tips: Traffic can be slow at peak times
Book Waiheke ferries and restaurants on sunny weekends
Weather changes quickly; carry a light shell

cities.name: Wellington
cities.tagline: Compact capital of harbour hills, cafes, museums, and film craft
cities.general: Wellington compresses parliament, museums, coffee, craft beer, hillside walks, and a working harbour into a walkable capital. It is also the ferry link between the North and South Islands.
activities: Ride the cable car to the Botanic Garden
tips: Wind is part of the experience; pack a shell
Cook Strait ferries need advance booking with vehicles
Central Wellington is easy without a car

cities.name: Christchurch
cities.tagline: Garden city rebuilt with creativity and Canterbury access
cities.general: Christchurch blends botanic gardens, new architecture, markets, street art, and easy access to Banks Peninsula, Arthur's Pass, and the Canterbury high country.
activities: Punt or walk along the Avon
Day-trip to Akaroa or Arthur's Pass
tips: Layer for cool evenings even in summer
Book rental cars early in peak South Island season
Road trips west can be affected by alpine weather

cities.name: Queenstown
cities.tagline: Alpine lake base for adventure, wine, and Great Walks
cities.general: Queenstown sits on Lake Wakatipu beneath the Remarkables, with jet boats, gondola views, wineries, ski fields, and access to Routeburn, Fiordland, and Mount Aspiring landscapes.
activities: Use town as a Great Walks base
tips: Accommodation prices spike in ski season and summer
Book Milford and Routeburn logistics early
Mountain weather changes fast

cities.name: Rotorua
cities.tagline: Geothermal lakes, Maori culture, and forest trails
cities.general: Rotorua is known for geothermal valleys, steaming lakes, Maori cultural experiences, and mountain-bike trails in Whakarewarewa Forest. It is a strong North Island nature and culture stop.
activities: Experience a cultural performance and hangi
tips: Geothermal steam has a sulphur smell around town
Book cultural evenings ahead
Forest trails drain well but can be muddy after rain

cities.name: Dunedin
cities.tagline: Southern heritage city with wildlife-rich Otago Peninsula
cities.general: Dunedin combines Scottish-influenced streets, student energy, railway architecture, surf beaches, and Otago Peninsula wildlife. It is a rewarding southern city stop before the Catlins or Central Otago.
activities: Look for albatross and penguins on Otago Peninsula
tips: Wildlife viewing is best with low-impact guided operators
Coastal weather can be cool and windy
Respect closed beach areas during nesting season

cities.name: Nelson
cities.tagline: Sunny arts town near Abel Tasman beaches and alpine parks
cities.general: Nelson is a sunny South Island base for galleries, markets, wineries, Abel Tasman beaches, and inland alpine parks. It works well for slower coastal travel and Great Walk logistics.
activities: Browse Saturday market and local galleries
Taste wine around Moutere or Mapua
Walk to the Centre of New Zealand viewpoint
tips: Summer accommodation fills early
Book Abel Tasman water taxis in advance
A car helps connect beaches, wineries, and trailheads

cities.name: Wanaka
cities.tagline: Lakeside mountain town for day hikes and Mount Aspiring access
cities.general: Wanaka is a calmer alpine-lake base than Queenstown, with day hikes, ski fields, bike trails, and access to Mount Aspiring National Park. It suits outdoors-focused road trips through Otago.
activities: Walk Mount Iron or Roys Peak
tips: Roys Peak is exposed; start early and carry water
Winter roads may require chains
Trailhead parking can fill before sunrise

cities.name: Broome
cities.tagline: Kimberley beach town of red cliffs, pearls, and sunset camels
cities.general: Broome sits on the Indian Ocean edge of the Kimberley, known for Cable Beach sunsets, pearling history, red pindan cliffs, dinosaur footprints, and long dry-season road trips into remote north-west Australia.
activities: Use Broome as a Kimberley road-trip base
tips: The dry season is busiest and most comfortable
Book tours and 4WD hire early
Check tide times for coastal sights

cities.name: Exmouth
cities.tagline: Ningaloo Reef base for whale sharks, beaches, and canyon country
cities.general: Exmouth is the main northern gateway to Ningaloo Reef and Cape Range National Park, pairing coral snorkel beaches with red limestone gorges and seasonal whale shark tours.
activities: Join a whale shark or manta ray tour
tips: Marine wildlife seasons vary by month
Carry water and shade for Cape Range walks
Book reef tours well ahead in peak season

cities.name: Margaret River
cities.tagline: Wine, surf, karri forest, caves, and the Cape to Cape coast
cities.general: Margaret River is a south-west base for vineyards, surf breaks, limestone caves, tall forest, local produce, and the Cape to Cape Track between two Indian Ocean lighthouses.
activities: Visit Lake Cave or Mammoth Cave
Walk a Cape to Cape section
tips: A car is useful for wineries and beaches
Book cellar doors and restaurants on weekends
Spring brings wildflowers and cooler walking weather

cities.name: Airlie Beach
cities.tagline: Whitsundays harbour town for island sailing and reef flights
cities.general: Airlie Beach is the mainland hub for the Whitsunday Islands, with marina departures for sailing trips, Whitehaven Beach, reef flights, and relaxed lagoon-side evenings.
tips: Book sailing trips ahead in school holidays
Marine stinger suits are common in warmer months
Cyclone season can disrupt plans

cities.name: Katoomba
cities.tagline: Blue Mountains town for sandstone lookouts and canyon walks
cities.general: Katoomba is the best-known Blue Mountains base, close to the Three Sisters, cliff-edge walks, waterfalls, heritage guesthouses, and multi-day tracks heading toward Jenolan Caves.
activities: See the Three Sisters from Echo Point
Walk the Prince Henry Cliff Walk
tips: Weekend trains from Sydney can be busy
Cliff weather can turn cold and misty
Carry a headlamp for longer valley walks

cities.name: Townsville
cities.tagline: Dry tropics city for Magnetic Island and reef-country access
cities.general: Townsville combines a dry tropical waterfront with Castle Hill views, museums, reef gateways, and ferries to Magnetic Island's beaches, koalas, forts, and granite headlands.
activities: Ride the ferry to Magnetic Island
Visit the Museum of Tropical Queensland
tips: Magnetic Island buses connect key bays
Summer heat is intense
Check marine stinger advice before swimming

cities.name: Launceston
cities.tagline: Northern Tasmania base for Cataract Gorge and Tamar Valley
cities.general: Launceston is a compact northern Tasmanian city near Cataract Gorge, heritage streets, Tamar Valley vineyards, and road routes to Cradle Mountain and the east coast.
activities: Taste wine in the Tamar Valley
Use the city as a Cradle Mountain gateway
tips: Winter mornings are cold
A car helps connect vineyards and parks
Book Cradle Mountain shuttles and accommodation ahead

cities.name: Port Douglas
cities.tagline: Tropical resort town between reef boats and Daintree rainforest
cities.general: Port Douglas is a relaxed Far North Queensland base with Four Mile Beach, marina reef departures, Sunday markets, and easy access to Mossman Gorge and the Daintree.
activities: Join a Great Barrier Reef cruise
tips: Reef trips are weather dependent
Book restaurants in peak dry season
Respect crocodile and stinger warnings

parks.name: Fiordland National Park
parks.tagline: Rainforest fiords, Great Walks, waterfalls, and alpine passes
parks.summary: Fiordland National Park protects New Zealand's largest wilderness of deep fiords, beech forest, waterfalls, lakes, and famous Great Walks including Milford, Routeburn, and Kepler.

parks.name: Tongariro National Park
parks.tagline: Volcanic plateau of sacred peaks, crater lakes, and alpine crossings
parks.summary: Tongariro National Park is a dual World Heritage landscape of active volcanoes, lava fields, emerald lakes, alpine tussock, and Maori cultural significance.

parks.name: Aoraki Mount Cook National Park
parks.tagline: New Zealand's highest mountain, glaciers, and starry alpine valleys
parks.summary: Aoraki Mount Cook National Park surrounds New Zealand's highest peak with glaciers, alpine valleys, day walks, mountaineering history, and dark-sky viewing.

parks.name: Abel Tasman National Park
parks.tagline: Golden beaches, kayak coves, and an easy coastal Great Walk
parks.summary: Abel Tasman National Park is New Zealand's smallest national park but one of its most accessible, with beaches, forested headlands, tidal estuaries, kayaking, and the Abel Tasman Coast Track.

parks.name: Mount Aspiring National Park
parks.tagline: Southern Alps valleys, glaciers, and trailheads near Wanaka
parks.summary: Mount Aspiring National Park links beech forest, braided rivers, glaciers, and high passes between Wanaka, Haast, and the Routeburn country.

parks.name: Karijini National Park
parks.tagline: Pilbara gorges, red rock pools, and ancient banded iron ranges
parks.summary: Karijini National Park protects deep red gorges, waterfalls, swimming holes, and layered iron formations in Western Australia's Pilbara.

parks.name: Kosciuszko National Park

hikes.name: Overland Track
hikes.tagline: 65 km alpine traverse from Cradle Mountain to Lake St Clair
hikes.summary: The Overland Track is Tasmania's signature multi-day walk, crossing alpine moorland, dolerite peaks, rainforest, waterfalls, and glacial lakes between Cradle Mountain and Lake St Clair.
tips: Bookings are required in the main walking season
Carry full wet-weather gear even in summer
Side trips add time and exposure
hikes.start_instructions: Most walkers start at Ronny Creek near Cradle Mountain and finish at Lake St Clair, using booked huts or tent platforms along the route.

hikes.name: Larapinta Trail
hikes.tagline: 223 km Red Centre traverse through the West MacDonnell Ranges
hikes.summary: The Larapinta Trail links Alice Springs with Mount Sonder through desert ridges, waterholes, ochre cliffs, and big-sky camps in the West MacDonnell Ranges.
tips: Walk in the cooler months from May to September
Water logistics define each stage
Avoid exposed climbs during heat
hikes.start_instructions: Traditional east-to-west itineraries begin at Alice Springs Telegraph Station and finish with an early climb of Mount Sonder.

hikes.name: Cape to Cape Track
hikes.tagline: Coastal walk between Cape Naturaliste and Cape Leeuwin
hikes.summary: The Cape to Cape Track follows limestone cliffs, beaches, karri forest pockets, and surf breaks along Western Australia's Margaret River coast.
tips: Soft sand sections are tiring
Wildflowers peak in spring
Arrange end-to-end transport before starting
hikes.start_instructions: Walkers usually start at either lighthouse; north-to-south itineraries finish at Cape Leeuwin near Augusta.

hikes.name: Great Ocean Walk
hikes.tagline: Clifftop and beach walk from Apollo Bay to the Twelve Apostles
hikes.summary: The Great Ocean Walk threads forests, beaches, river mouths, campsites, and limestone cliffs along Victoria's famous shipwreck coast.
tips: Check tide times for beach sections
Pre-book campsites or luggage transfers
Weather can be windy on exposed headlands
hikes.start_instructions: The official route starts at Apollo Bay and heads west toward the Twelve Apostles visitor area.

hikes.name: Six Foot Track
hikes.tagline: Historic Blue Mountains track from Katoomba to Jenolan Caves
hikes.summary: The Six Foot Track follows an 1880s bridle route through gullies, farmland, suspension bridges, and ridgelines between Katoomba and Jenolan Caves.
tips: Carry water between camps
Check Jenolan road access before arranging pickup
Expect steep climbs out of valleys
hikes.start_instructions: Most walkers begin near Katoomba's Explorers Tree and arrange transport from Jenolan Caves.

hikes.name: Routeburn Track
hikes.tagline: Alpine Great Walk between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland
hikes.summary: The Routeburn Track crosses beech forest, waterfalls, alpine tarns, and the Harris Saddle between the Queenstown and Te Anau sides of the Southern Alps.
tips: Huts book out quickly
Transport is needed between trailheads
Snow and avalanche hazards affect shoulder seasons
hikes.start_instructions: Walkers commonly start at Routeburn Shelter near Glenorchy and finish at The Divide on the Milford Road.

hikes.name: Milford Track
hikes.tagline: Classic Fiordland Great Walk to Milford Sound
hikes.summary: The Milford Track follows lake, river, rainforest, and alpine pass terrain from Lake Te Anau toward Milford Sound, including Mackinnon Pass and Sutherland Falls side trips.
tips: Great Walk bookings sell out fast
Heavy rain can flood sections
Boat and bus transfers are part of the route
hikes.start_instructions: The managed walk starts with a boat transfer to Glade Wharf and finishes with a boat from Sandfly Point near Milford Sound.

hikes.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
hikes.tagline: Volcanic day walk past crater lakes and lava fields
hikes.summary: The Tongariro Alpine Crossing traverses exposed volcanic terrain between Mangatepopo and Ketetahi, with crater rims, emerald lakes, steam vents, and huge plateau views.
tips: Use shuttle transport; parking is restricted
Go only in suitable weather
Winter conditions require alpine gear and experience
hikes.start_instructions: Most hikers use shuttle services from National Park or Turangi to start at Mangatepopo and finish at Ketetahi.

hikes.name: Abel Tasman Coast Track
hikes.tagline: Beach-hopping Great Walk with tidal crossings and water taxis
hikes.summary: The Abel Tasman Coast Track links golden beaches, forested headlands, estuaries, and campsites along one of New Zealand's sunniest coastlines.
tips: Time tidal crossings carefully
Water taxis make flexible section walks possible
Book huts and campsites in summer
hikes.start_instructions: Most walkers begin at Marahau and use water taxis or road transport around the northern trailhead.

hikes.name: Kepler Track
hikes.tagline: Fiordland circuit of lake shore, beech forest, and alpine ridges
hikes.summary: The Kepler Track is a purpose-built Fiordland circuit from near Te Anau, climbing from lakeshore forest to long alpine ridge walking and descending through wetlands.
tips: Alpine sections are exposed to wind
Huts require Great Walk bookings
The track can be shortened with transport to control gates
hikes.start_instructions: The usual circuit starts near Te Anau at the Kepler Track car park or control gates.

hikes.name: Hooker Valley Track
hikes.tagline: Glacial valley walk to Aoraki Mount Cook viewpoints
hikes.summary: The Hooker Valley Track is an accessible out-and-back walk from White Horse Hill to swing bridges, glacier views, and Aoraki Mount Cook framed above Hooker Lake.
tips: Start early for calmer weather and parking
Stay on marked boardwalks
Cloud can hide Aoraki quickly
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the White Horse Hill campground and follow the signed valley track to Hooker Lake.

hikes.name: Three Capes Track
hikes.tagline: Clifftop Tasman Peninsula walk with dolerite sea stacks
hikes.summary: The Three Capes Track follows the Tasman Peninsula's dramatic sea cliffs, heathland, coastal forest, and dolerite columns between Cape Pillar and Cape Hauy.
tips: Bookings are required for the hut-based itinerary
Weather can be windy and exposed
Carry layers even in summer
hikes.start_instructions: The managed walk starts from Port Arthur with transport and finishes near Fortescue Bay.

hikes.name: Bibbulmun Track
hikes.tagline: Western Australia end-to-end walk from Perth hills to Albany
hikes.summary: The Bibbulmun Track traverses jarrah, karri, tingle forest, farmland, rivers, and wild southern coastline between Kalamunda and Albany.
tips: End-to-end walkers need careful food drops
Spring wildflowers are a highlight
Huts are basic and first-come, first-served
hikes.start_instructions: The northern terminus is in Kalamunda near Perth; the southern terminus is in Albany.

hikes.name: Heysen Trail
hikes.tagline: South Australian traverse from Cape Jervis to the Flinders Ranges
hikes.summary: The Heysen Trail links beaches, vineyards, forests, farmland, and rugged ranges from the Fleurieu Peninsula to Parachilna Gorge.
tips: Northern sections close during fire danger season
Water and resupply planning are essential
Walk cooler months for exposed range country
hikes.start_instructions: Most section walkers choose shorter legs; end-to-end hikers usually walk north in cooler months.

hikes.name: Australian Alps Walking Track
hikes.tagline: High-country traverse through Victoria, New South Wales, and ACT
hikes.summary: The Australian Alps Walking Track links alpine national parks, snow gums, ridgelines, huts, and remote high-country terrain from Walhalla to Canberra.
tips: Navigation and self-sufficiency are required
Snow can persist on high sections
Food drops simplify long remote stretches
hikes.start_instructions: The official route runs between Walhalla in Victoria and Tharwa near Canberra.

hikes.name: Jatbula Trail
hikes.tagline: Top End escarpment walk from Nitmiluk Gorge to Edith Falls
hikes.summary: The Jatbula Trail follows Jawoyn country across sandstone escarpment, monsoon pockets, swimming holes, waterfalls, and open woodland in Nitmiluk National Park.
tips: Permits and campsites are limited
Walk in the dry season
Heat and water planning matter every day
hikes.start_instructions: Walkers cross the Katherine River by boat from Nitmiluk Gorge and finish at Leliyn / Edith Falls.

hikes.name: Thorsborne Trail
hikes.tagline: Remote Hinchinbrook Island rainforest, beaches, and peaks
hikes.summary: The Thorsborne Trail crosses Hinchinbrook Island's beaches, mangroves, rainforest, creeks, and mountain views between Ramsay Bay and George Point.
tips: Permits are strictly limited
Tide timing affects creek and beach sections
Pack for wet tropical conditions
hikes.start_instructions: Boat transfers connect the trailheads with Cardwell or Lucinda depending on direction.

hikes.name: Kosciuszko Main Range Walk
hikes.tagline: Alpine loop over Australia's highest summit
hikes.summary: The Main Range Walk loops through alpine herbfields, glacial lakes, ridges, and Mount Kosciuszko's summit above Thredbo and Charlotte Pass.
tips: Summer weather can still be cold and exposed
Carry sun and wind protection
Snow changes the route in winter and spring
hikes.start_instructions: The loop commonly starts and finishes at Charlotte Pass, crossing the Snowy River stepping stones.

hikes.name: Wineglass Bay Lookout Track
hikes.tagline: Short Freycinet climb to the classic Wineglass Bay view
hikes.summary: The Wineglass Bay Lookout Track climbs from Coles Bay through granite slopes and coastal bush to the postcard view over Wineglass Bay.
tips: Arrive early for parking
Steps are steep in places
Continue to the beach only if you have extra time
hikes.start_instructions: Start at the signed Freycinet car park near Coles Bay and follow the lookout track.
